audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers agree with each other but disagree with the packet chart and with their own whys[]. The page gives Akshan Levels 1-3 and calls 4-5, 6, first item and 2+ items 'Skill', while whys[0] says level 1 is 'a true coinflip start' and whys[6] says Neeko out-scales at two items.
audit.why: Level 1 is written as even but rendered as an Akshan win, and the late game is written as a Neeko win but rendered as Skill — the row that the 80% win rate actually comes from.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Neeko, matching the packet and the existing whys, proposed as matched full/content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3] through phases[6] carried boilerplate that names no Akshan ability and describes spikes that do not exist in this lane ('Stormsurge spike — a rooted target loses half their HP').
audit.why: The real shape is: he owns 3-5 on Avengerang range and Heroic Swing, holds the edge through first item, and loses the scaling once Neeko's AoE comes online.
audit.corrected: phases[2] through phases[6] rewritten on Heroic Swing (18/16.5/15/13.5/12s), Avengerang, the hidden Pop Blossom wind-up, and the two-item AoE flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] and mid tell you to set up Pop Blossom 'while disguised or invisible (W)' and to 'pop W to go invisible'. Neeko's Shapesplitter has no invisibility in its description — it sends a clone and recasts to redirect it. The camouflage in this matchup belongs to Akshan's Going Rogue (W). Nothing on the page mentioned Dirty Fighting (P), which shields him every third hit.
audit.why: A player told they have invisibility will walk in with a clone out and die. And the shield is exactly what eats a Neeko burst window.
audit.corrected: Invisibility claims replaced with the real mechanic — Inherent Glamour hides the Pop Blossom preparation while disguised. dontsFull[0].d now states the Dirty Fighting shield. report[5].t gives the 18s Heroic Swing cooldown and the champion/terrain collision that ends the swing.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d offers a 'fifteen-second invitation' after Heroic Swing.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s — fifteen seconds is only true at rank 3.

edits.before: Open disguised as something harmless — the first Q trade lands while Akshan is still reading the wave.
edits.after: Neither of you has a combo — Blooming Burst re-blooms off the minions he hides behind, so it's an even start.

edits.before: Full kit: E root through a minion into double-bloom Q is your core chunk. The root stretches longer through targets.
edits.after: Heroic Swing lets him leave your one telegraphed root on reaction, so he pokes Avengerang freely while E finds nothing.

edits.before: Trade Q on his CS timings and hold E for the step-up. The disguise resets every bad position you take.
edits.after: Avengerang out-ranges you and Heroic Swing dodges your one root — farm with Q and bank for level 6.

edits.before: Pop Blossom online — your all-in is a setup puzzle: E root, walk in as a clone or minion, R the panic.
edits.after: Pop Blossom's wind-up is hidden while disguised — set it up unseen and slam the moment he commits a swing.

edits.before: Stormsurge spike — a rooted target now loses half their HP to one rotation.
edits.after: His first item keeps the kite duel his — don't force the sidelane 1v1 yet.

edits.before: You're the teamfight flank now: disguise, walk into the clump, and R three people. Lane leads become fight wins.
edits.after: Your AoE out-scales his single-target kit — flank the clump and your Q-into-R deletes his squishy frame.

edits.before: Akshan burns Heroic Swing on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Akshan burns Heroic Swing on nothing — that's an 18-second invitation at rank 1.

edits.before: That’s Akshan’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Every third hit of Dirty Fighting shields him — trade in bursts, never in autos.

edits.before: Track Akshan’s Heroic Swing: His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and champions or terrain knock him off it mid-swing — body-block the line, then step up.

edits.before: Set up R (Pop Blossom) while disguised or invisible (W) so he never sees the channel coming to interrupt it
edits.after: Set up R (Pop Blossom) while disguised — Inherent Glamour hides the preparation, so he never sees it coming at all

edits.before: Levels 4-5 still belong to him — he pokes from range I can't match and swings out of anything I throw, so I farm with Q waveclear and bank for 6 rather than forcing a losing all-in. Level 6 is where I answer: I can disguise as an ally or pop W to go invisible, set up Pop Blossom unseen, and slam down for the stun the instant he commits a swing. If my E lands first, the root removes his mobility and the R stun chains into a Q re-bloom that bursts his squishy frame — that one connected combo is a kill. Bait his E-swing out, then catch him mid-animation.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 still belong to him — he pokes from range you can't match and swings out of anything you throw, so farm with Q waveclear and bank for 6 rather than forcing a losing all-in. Level 6 is your answer: disguise as an ally, and because Inherent Glamour hides the Pop Blossom preparation entirely, slam down for the stun the instant he commits a swing. If E lands first, the root takes his mobility and the R stun chains into a Q re-bloom that bursts his squishy frame — that one combo is a kill. Bait Heroic Swing out, then catch him mid-animation.

notes: The packet defect was real: the chart gave Akshan 5 of 7 stages behind an 80% win rate, and the two layers agreed with each other while both disagreeing with their own whys[] on Level 1 and on 2+ items. Fixed to the packet order in matched pairs. The invisibility claim in wants.you[1] and mid was the dangerous one — Neeko's Shapesplitter description contains no invisibility, only a clone with a directional recast; camouflage in this lane is Akshan's Going Rogue. Per the mirror, the correct mechanic is that Inherent Glamour hides Pop Blossom's preparation while disguised. I did NOT write the missingInteractions 'dash-denied' item: neither Going Rogue nor Heroic Swing carries anything in Riot's text that denies a dash, and Pop Blossom is a leap from a preparation rather than a dash Akshan can interact with.
